You didn’t notice it, but Ramos on the first goal ran towards keeper to pull both defenders deep. This created that space for Cisse. Ramos 5.5 is insanity, he actually helped with both goals quite well

Don’t mind all these ones that their eyes are covered by his Price Tag and not his movements. You could clearly see he was point that Rabiot gives it to Cisse. If the othwr players were a bit more aware of what’s arount them, he probably would score more.. But we have players that on the final third most of the time, they usually only see the limelight.. He doea have his fault though which he is never in the box.. but that could be by design.

Ramos isn’t a midfielder, he’s supposed to be the 9, a central striker, the point man at the tip of the spear, the guy who’s #1 job is to SCORE, and #2 job is to hold up the ball. He should always be in the box! What’s worse is that when he does get the ball in the box, he’s too slow, clumsy, and lacking in ball skills, whatever, to get a really good shot off to score. He had a chance in the opening moments of the game and couldn’t get his feet set up to get off a decent shot! And THAT is why he passed to Pulisic rather than try to take another shot. He knew he was going to muff another really good chance on goal. Ramos plays like a midfielder who does almost nothing other than sort of fake pressing (when have you EVER seen him nick the ball off a opponent and start a key transition, like Pulisic did?), and then making all those “runs to pull away the defense”. Come on, you do NOT spend €74 million for a player to do stuff that ANY PLAYER can do on the pitch!!!

There are a lot of nuances, which you aren’t picking up on apparently.

Name me 5 instances of service that he received that he didn’t score from? i’m struggling to recall five all season. He feeds on scraps. He gets no decent service. He has to play as an AM just to help create something. And even though we didn’t bring him in to pull defenders for others to score, he is at least doing that.

You have to take his performances with a grain of salt.

Herean instance for you. Why did he pass it to Pulisic instead of shooting? A true striker buries that opportunity without even thinking. He is a PSG sub and a tap in merchant. I am sorry.

Spot on again. Lack of service is a Milan way of life. It’s probably because the supporting cast has always been hell bent on trying to score. Leao, Pulisic, and now Moreira, Hutchinson and Cisse are players who look to score first, not to assist.

Re-read my post. We’re saying the same thing vis-a-vis Ramos. I’m not one of the ones who is against him. I think maybe we overpaid, but as it stand I think he’s doing alright overall, and I think he’ll eventually start scoring.

As to Puli and Moreira, I’m nitpicking! Chill. Glad the ball ended up in the back of the net.

I honestly don’t put too much stock into what any coach does at Man U, Chelsea or Milan (sadly). Those clubs have all been run so poorly for an extended period of time that there is only so much a coach can do there.

#1945. ‘Big prospect’ – Teddy Sheringham urges Man Utd to sign £30m Brighton star ahead of Arsenal

Teddy Sheringham believes Manchester United should look to sign Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas to add more firepower to their side.

The Red Devils currently sit 18th in the Premier League table and without a win in eight matches in the competition after their dramatic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa last weekend.

And that disappointing start to the season appears set to cost Michael Carrick his job, with the latest reports suggesting the 45-year-old will be sacked over the international break.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

But former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino has now emerged as a serious candidate to replace Carrick before their match against Liverpool on November 22.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Regardless of who ultimately replaces Carrick, Sheringham believes the new United manager will need support in the transfer market to turn his former club’s fortunes around.

In particular, the former England striker believes the Red Devils could do with some more attacking firepower, name-checking young Brighton striker Kostoulas as his ideal target in the January window.

‘There’s one player I’d like to see Manchester United go and sign in January and it’s the young Greek centre-forward at Brighton, Charalampos Kostoulas,’ Sheringham told Metro. ‘What a player he is. I love him.

‘I love the way he plays. He’s got energy, he knows his position, and he’s still a young man as well.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He knows how to retain possession, and he definitely knows where the net is. He brings players into play, and has got that bit of flair about him.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Kostoulas, who arrived from Olympiakos for £30million in June 2025, has five goal contributions in ten league matches this season to help his side sit second in the table.

The Greek teenager scored in Brighton’s impressive 3-0 win over Arsenal in September, and Sheringham believes United may have to fend off interest from the Gunners to sign the 19-year-old.

‘I think he’ll be the next centre-forward to go for big money,’ Sheringham, speaking via Boyle Sports, added.

‘I’d be surprised if Arsenal don’t go for him before United have a chance so United need to get him in quickly.

‘For me, he’s the next big prospect coming through in world football, and you’ve got to get him in to lead the line.

‘I know he’s only a young lad but he’s just got that stature about him, and he’s full of confidence. Confidence is a massive thing. He’s playing with confidence right now and at the moment he looks fantastic.’

#1944. Slovenia vs Switzerland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 11:29, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 19:02

Switzerland will be bidding to secure first spot in Group B1 and automatic promotion to League A when they continue their UEFA Nations League campaign on Friday against Slovenia.

National Team have been perfect in the 2026-27 tournament, collecting 12 points from four matches, and they will be facing a Slovenia side that are second in the section.

Slovenia boast a record of two wins, one draw and one defeat from their four matches in Group B1, with seven points representing a solid return.

Bostjan Cesar's side are three points ahead of third-placed Scotland and five behind the leaders Switzerland, demonstrating the need for them to secure a win on Friday night.

Slovenia, as it stands, are in a promotion playoff spot, but they could still finish first or third, with two games left to play, heading to North Macedonia after this one.

The hosts picked up four points from their first two games in the section, drawing 0-0 with Scotland before recording a 2-0 win over North Macedonia; a 2-1 defeat to Switzerland followed, and they then recorded a 2-1 victory over Scotland last time out.

Slovenia have only won two of their previous 12 matches against Switzerland in all competitions, with their last success over Friday's opponents coming in October 2014.

Switzerland are certain of a top-two spot in the section, but it would be a shock if they passed up first position and automatic promotion to League A from such a strong position.

National Team are top of Group B1 on 12 points, and they have been impressive in the tournament, opening up with a 3-0 win over North Macedonia, before recording a 3-0 victory over Scotland in their second away game in the section.

Murat Yakin's side then won back-to-back home fixtures in October, beating Slovenia 2-1 and North Macedonia 3-0 to take complete control of the section.

Switzerland were beaten by Argentina in the quarter-finals of the 2026 World Cup, but they have won eight of their last nine matches and will once again be the favourites here.

National Team will finish their Group B1 campaign at home to Scotland on November 16.

Slovenia will be without the services of two players through suspension on Friday, with David Zec and Erik Janza missing due to an accumulation of yellow cards.

Benjamin Sesko is another notable absentee for the home side; the Manchester United striker remains unavailable with a shin injury and is not expected back until early 2027.

Swansea City's Zan Vipotnik started through the middle against Scotland last time out, and the 24-year-old is expected to keep hold of his spot in the XI for this match.

Switzerland, meanwhile, have no suspension issues, although a booking for Michel Aebischer in this match would see him ruled out of the team's final group fixture.

There are not expected to be any major surprises in the away side's lineup for this match, with Remo Freuler and Dan Ndoye among those set to be in the starting side.

Meanwhile, there should be a spot through the middle for Zeki Amdouni, who has scored 14 times in 37 appearances for his country.

However, Johan Manzambi has returned to Aston Villa and will therefore not be involved due to a calf issue.

Oblak; Karnicnik, Brekalo, Bijol, Drkusic, Kuzmic; Matko, Zabukovnik, Gnezda Cerin, Sturm; Vipotnik

Kobel; Britschgi, Elvedi, Akanji, Rodriguez; Freuler, Zakaria; Sow, Rieder, Ndoye; Amdouni

This is shaping up to be a fascinating battle in the Nations League; it would not be a surprise to see the points shared, but we just have a feeling that Switzerland could edge a close match to continue their perfect record in the 2026-27 tournament.

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Spain will hope to maintain their 100 winning per cent record in the 2026/27 Nations League when they face the Czech Republic this evening.

Spain sit top of Group A3 courtesy of their 3-2 win against England at Wembley at the start of their Nations League campaign, enough to place La Roja three points above the Three Lions with two games remaining.

If Spain and England record expected wins against the Czech Republic and Croatia, respectively, then Sunday’s clash between the two teams will decide who enjoys seeded status in the draw for the quarter finals.

The hosts are led by Spaniard Santi Denia, who became the first foreigner to manage the Czech Republic after his appointment in the summer.

Denia’s side were unable to put up much of a fight in the reverse fixture, falling to a 3-1 defeat in Oviedo and seeing Ladislav Krejci dismissed five minutes from time.

Without a win in their four games in the Nations League so far this campaign, the Czechs need to find points from somewhere to stave off relegation to the competition’s second tier.

#1942. Alex Baena urges Arsenal star to join Atletico Madrid: ‘He’s the second best in the world’

Alex Baena has urged Atletico Madrid to sign Martin Zubimendi and believes the Arsenal midfielder is the second best in the world behind Rodri.

Zubimendi joined Arsenal in a £60 million deal from Real Sociedad last year and the 27-year-old played an integral role in the team’s Premier League title success under Mikel Arteta last season.

However, Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game this term and now faces increased competition for a place in Arsenal’s midfield following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes in the summer transfer window.

Zubimendi has been linked with a move away from Arsenal ahead of the January transfer window and Chelsea are understood to have registered their interest.

Baena, who was also part of Spain’s World Cup success in the summer alongside Zubimendi, is keen to see his countryman return to La Liga.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

When asked about the prospect of Zubimendi joining Atletico, Baena told Cadena SER: ‘I would love for him to come.

‘He is the second best defensive midfielder in the world after Rodri.

‘I hope he can come. He would be a great addition to the team and the dressing room.’

Baena also spoke out on Arsenal’s summer transfer target Julian Alvarez, who pushed for a move to Barcelona but ended up staying at Atletico and received hostility from the club’s supporters.

#1941. Carlton Cole says Man Utd star should have been sold years ago: ‘He’s won the lottery!’

Carlton Cole says Diogo Dalot ‘won the lottery’ when he joined Manchester United and should have been sold years ago.

Dalot is one of the United’s longest-serving players, having made over 250 appearances for the Red Devils since his £19m move from Porto in 2018.

Former Manchester United boss Jose Mourinho hailed Dalot as the ‘best young full-back in Europe’ at the time but the Portugal international has attracted much criticism during his time at Old Trafford.

Dalot has endured a particularly poor couple of weeks, struggling in United’s Champions League win over Roma and Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

The 27-year-old was branded ‘atrocious’ after the Roma clash and was booed as he was subbed off by Michael Carrick against Villa.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Ex-England striker Cole is shocked Dalot is still at Manchester United and says the full-back ‘probably can’t believe his luck’.

‘It’s got to be down to Michael Carrick as well,’ Cole said on The Dressing Room podcast when discussing the huge issues at Old Trafford.

‘He’s playing certain personnel in that team that I’m thinking, “how are you even still there?” I’ve said it before but Diogo Dalot, how is he still there?

‘He’s way off it, he is way off it. You can’t depend on him. All he’s thinking about is his next pay check, that’s what’s going through his head.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He’s not worried about saving the gaffer’s job. He probably can’t believe his luck that he’s there, he’s playing at Old Trafford in front of those brilliant fans in a lovely stadium with all that history.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘For me, he’s won the lottery. I don’t know how he’s on that pitch. He keeps making the same mistakes and getting caught out, he was at fault last week and he was at fault again at the weekend.’

Manchester United fans cheered when Carrick prepared to sub off Dalot against Aston Villa and then booed as he made his way off the pitch.

Asked about that reaction after the game, Carrick said: ‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think. I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it.

‘We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed. And the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today. That’s, you know… he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake. But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything.

‘So I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group. I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking the team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision. But it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

An eighth league game without a win leaves Manchester United 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break.

A dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost Carrick his job at Old Trafford, with Eddie Howe the current frontrunner to take over.

#1939. South Africa vs Kenya - prediction, team news, lineups

By Byron David | 11 Nov 2026 11:42, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 18:07

South Africa will look to continue their post-World Cup momentum when they host Kenya in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Friday, November 13, at the Orlando Stadium in Johannesburg.

With the visitors already guaranteed a spot in next year's tournament as co-hosts, only one slot is open for qualification in Group D.

South Africa are coming off what was their best-ever display at a World Cup, as they progressed from the group to the knockouts for the first time in their history.

Bafana Bafana seem to be riding that wave of success, as they have won both of their opening AFCON qualifiers in the group.

The men in green and gold have achieved positive results from excellent performances, despite a huge change in their technical team.

Hugo Broos stepped down from his role, opening the door for Pitso Mosimane to return to the helm for his second stint as the national coach.

The players have responded positively to Mosimane, as they are unbeaten under his guidance during his second tenure, with South Africa beating Egypt last time out in an international friendly.

The 1996 AFCON champions are also the most potent side in the qualifying roster, scoring seven goals in two games at an average of 3.5 goals per match.

Having been unbeaten in their only two head-to-heads with Kenya, the hosts are expected to secure three points here and consolidate their position at the top of Group D.

Kenya are currently led by former South African forward Benni McCarthy, who is dealing with salary payment issues with his current employers.

Nonetheless, he has stated that he will maintain his professionalism and lead the Harambee Stars to Johannesburg this week.

The visitors have their work cut out for them, especially since they are winless in their opening two fixtures of qualifying, drawing their opener with Eritrea and losing their recent competitive fixture against Guinea.

Their results here have no bearing on their qualification, as they will feature in the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts; however, McCarthy still wants his men to gather momentum in preparation for their home tournament.

Kenya have not scored in five of their last 10 matches, while they have scored just twice in four previous meetings with South Africa.

South Africa Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Kenya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mosimane is sweating over the fitness of captain Ronwen Williams and Teboho Mokoena, but did mention that he will wait until the very end to see if the doctors will pass them fit.

Themba Zwane was left out of the squad, while Mbekezeli Mbokazi returns to the Bafana Bafana set-up for this double-header with the Harambee Stars.

It is fully expected that Mbokazi slots straight into the centre-back pairing alongside Ime Okon, with Thabang Matuludi and Aubrey Modiba likely to feature on either side of them.

Lyle Foster also earned a call-up after his move to Houston Dynamo, which means Mosimane likely wants to get a look at the former Burnley man.

The good news for the visiting side is the return of their captain Michael Olunga to the side after an injury, with Eric Ouma joining him.

Alpha Onyango was brought in for the injured Manzur Okwaro, but it will be interesting to see McCarthy tinker with his lineup to get a better idea of what his team looks like going forward.

Williams; Matuludi, Okon, Mbokazi, Modiba; Mokoena, Sithole; Appollis, Mofokeng, Puthejane; Foster

Omondi; Onyango, Harper, Odhiambo, Owino; Ochieng, Okwaro, Bajaber, Olunga; Ogam, Obiero

South Africa are in a positive space at the moment, having won each of their last three matches in all competitions, and they have never lost a match to Kenya in normal time.

The visitors' struggles in the final third has been a sore point for them, so it is easy to see the hosts shut Kenya off.

#1938. William Gallas says only one team can rival Arsenal for the Premier League title

William Gallas believes that only one team has the ability to rival Arsenal in this season’s Premier League title race.

Arsenal are now five points clear at the top of the league table following their hard-fought 1-0 win at home to Hull City on Saturday.

But it was another bad weekend for Manchester City as their third successive league defeat saw Enzo Maresca’s side slip to third.

Brighton are now second in the table as Fabian Hurzeler’s side continued their superb start to the season with a 2-0 win over Brentford.

The Seagulls have already beaten both Arsenal and City in the league this season, with no team scoring more goals and only Arsenal conceding fewer after ten games.

But despite that impressive start from Brighton, Gallas still expects City to come on strong and provide the only real test for Arsenal in the title race this campaign.

‘Right now, it looks like only those two teams, Arsenal and Manchester City, are really going to fight for the title.’

Gallas was also keen to rave about Arsenal’s superb defensive record once again this season, adding: ‘They have conceded just five goals, and that is going to be the question from everyone: how many goals will they concede this season?

#1935. Martin Zubimendi responds to Chelsea transfer speculation and reveals Mikel Arteta warning

Martin Zubimend has revealed he was warned he would face a fight to maintain his status as a regular starter at Arsenal this season, but insists he hasn’t given up hope of winning back his place.

The Spain international joined the Gunners 18 months ago following a £60million move from Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi had come close to signing for Liverpool a year earlier, but was convinced to snub the Reds’ interest and delay a move to England, with Mikel Arteta outlining his determination to make him a key component of his midfield rebuild.

The 27-year-old’s decision to move to the north London club initially looked an inspired one as he played almost every game over the course of the first two thirds of a campaign that ultimately ended in glory.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly during the run-in and he has been reduced to a bit-part role ever since.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Arsenal’s decision to sanction the signing of Bruno Guimaraes has only served to further heighten the intense competition for places and, as a result, Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game this season.

That lack of game time has sparked intense speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Chelsea, who are in the market for a midfielder and whose manager, Xabi Alonso, attempted to sign Zubimendi during his brief stint in charge of Real Madrid, are said to be considering renewing interest having made tentative enquiries during the summer.

Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, have been positioned as the frontrunners, with Diego Simeone said to be dreaming of signing the Arsenal star with reports in Spain going as far as saying that a deal is close.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to a whirlwind of rumours, Zubimendi told Marca: ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Asked whether his current predicament has come as a surprise, Zubimendi revealed Arteta had been totally transparent at the season’s outset and outlined the role he envisaged for a player he fought so hard to sign.

He said:  ‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.’

He added:  ‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1933. Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s replacement

Manchester United are close to rubber stamping a deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s successor ahead of making a final decision on the future of their current head coach.

The Red Devils are languishing in the relegation zone after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which is expected to represent Carrick’s final game at the helm, despite an injury-time comeback which yielded an unlikely point.

Carrick currently remains in limbo and attended United’s training ground on Wednesday morning with club executives set to discuss his future at a meeting in Monaco.

The 45-year-old was photographed driving into the club’s Carrington base this morning, but his fate is set to be determined at a meeting 800 miles away, where co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe will confer with United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

According to the Athletic, United’s key decision makers held talks on Tuesday and settled on Mauricio Pochettino as the candidate best qualified to lead the club out of the almost unprecedented mess it finds itself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager signed a contract with US Soccer through to 2030 just three months ago, and is currently preparing the American national side for CONCACAF Nations League matches against Haiti in the November international break.

The former Argentina international has held talks with United in the past and is keen on the job this time, but hefty compensation would be due to US Soccer.

United are understood to have been in contact with Pochettino’s representatives and although personal terms are unlikely to be an issue, the 54-year-old’s exit clause of £7.4million would need to be paid in full.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired, while ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were linked a fortnight ago when United seriously considered replacing Carrick.

Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away.

‘It’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events,’ Carrick said. ‘But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

‘Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

#1932. Gary Neville sends Mauricio Pochettino plea ahead of Manchester United appointment

Manchester United legend Gary Neville has urged incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to “protect himself” by demanding reinforcements in the January transfer window.

The Red Devils finally look set to appoint the Argentine almost eight years on from first speaking to the former Tottenham boss about the top job at Old Trafford.

With United sat in the Premier League relegation zone after 10 games, Michael Carrick was sacked, paving the way for Pochettino to take over in the north west.

But Neville has issued a warning to the newest managerial appointment, claiming Pochettino must receive guarantees of investment in the next few transfer windows.

Speaking on The Overlap’s Stick to Football, Neville said: “I’m sure Mauricio Pochettino is doing this, but if you were coming into this job now - you’ve talked about don’t believe an owner on the way in about what they’re going to spend, moving the goalposts - if I were Mauricio Pochettino now, I would literally be protecting myself to the high heaven.

“He’ll do that with the payoff. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he’s got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He’s got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around.”

United have largely restricted their major overhauls to summer transfer windows in recent seasons, attempting to improve their strikeforce in 2025 before bringing in midfield reinforcements this year.

#1929. How Manchester United could line up in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game against Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino is set to take charge at Manchester United as Michael Carrick’s replacement, leading fans to speculate on what his first starting XI will look like.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, November 22.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival.

Interestingly, Pochettino might be tempted to copy Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back. Out of possession the right-back tucks in to form a three-man defence in Pochettino’s favoured system, but with an actual left-back fit, there is little reason to play defenders out of position.

For that reason, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach. Yoro and Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence could give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu seems a strong fit at left-back. Antonee Robinson loved to get forward for Pochettino while on USA duty, and the wing-back is a proven attacking threat.

With the USA, Pochettino has settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

However, with United’s striking options limited, it would not be a surprise to see Mbeumo lead the line, with Amad Diallo playing instead on the right.

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 12:20, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 12:23

Manchester United have reportedly reached an agreement in principle with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, should Michael Carrick be sacked.

The club's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future at the helm.

The expectation is that Wilcox and Berrada will recommend Carrick is removed from his position as head coach due to the team's ongoing struggles.

The report claims that the 20-time English champions are willing to pay the £7.4m required to release Pochettino from his contract with the United States.

Meanwhile, the club are also said to be prepared to pay compensation in order to ensure that Pochettino can bring his trusted staff members with him to Old Trafford.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup.

Carrick took Man United training on Tuesday and has again been at Carrington on Wednesday amid the uncertainty surrounding his future.

At this stage, no confirmation has arrived in terms of a change of head coach, but the expectation is that the Englishman will lose his job over the next 24 hours or so.

Pochettino, who has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, is said to be incredibly keen on the Man United job.

The Argentine's first game in charge of the 20-time English champions is set to be the trip to Anfield to tackle Liverpool in the Premier League on November 22.

A difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign has left the Red Devils down in 18th spot in the Premier League table.

#1927. Danny Murphy tells Liverpool to explore transfer move for £33m Man Utd target

Danny Murphy has urged Liverpool to strongly consider a transfer move for Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde this winter.

Liverpool invested heavily in the summer with a view to giving Andoni Iraola the best possible chance in the hot seat following Arne Slot’s dismissal as manager.

It saw Jeremy Jacquet, Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz all added to Iraola’s squad for a combined fee of around £200million – and the trio have gone on to enjoy encouraging starts to life at Anfield.

With the Reds having dropped points in five of their opening ten matches of the Premier League campaign, though, attentions have quickly turned to the January transfer window as an opportunity to further strengthen.

Milos Kerkez has blown hot and cold since joining Liverpool for a fee of £40million from Bournemouth 18 months ago and rumours have been circulating that the club could reenter the transfer market for a new left-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Merseyside giants have been credited with a strong interest in Juventus’ Andrea Cambiaso and Santos’ Vinicius Lira in recent days, with Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas both yet to fully convince fans that they could eventually fill the shoes left by Andy Robertson.

But according to Murphy, ‘super talent’ Balde could be the ideal signing for Liverpool given the out-of-favour Spaniard is already used to the expectations that come with playing for a ‘huge football club’.

Balde has made just three substitute appearances for Barca in La Liga this term and Manchester United have also been named as a potential escape route for the £33m-rated defender at the halfway point of the season.

‘I think Liverpool will be looking for a left-back but it’s hard because I don’t know Kerkez personally, I know he’s trying really hard and you can see it in his energy that he cares, and that’s a great start,’ the ex-Liverpool and England midfielder told Betarades.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He cares for the shirt and he’s working really hard to try and make it happen.

‘I think Balde could be great for Liverpool because he’s a super talent and he’s also got that experience of being at a huge football club with that expectation.

‘Balde’s a really good player. There’s lots of good players out there and Liverpool will be scouring the world.’

Murphy believes it could be time for Liverpool to look for ‘more established’ and ‘ready-made players’ after prioritising youth in recent transfer windows.

‘I think the most important thing is trying to bring somebody in who doesn’t make you guess whether he can deal with the pressure of a big club,’ he added.

‘It’s a delicate balance because Liverpool for years were very good at taking diamonds in from the rough, if you like. Someone like [Philippe] Coutinho, like [Andy] Robertson, like [Sadio] Mane even from Southampton. [Roberto] Firmino was about £20m.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool took those diamonds in the rough and moulded them into these superstars, and then when we’ve tried to go and spend massive money on these already made stars, it’s not quite worked.

‘I still think there are times, especially in defensive areas where you really do want ready-made players. Especially when you’re struggling.

‘I think Liverpool have got enough young players now who need to grow. I think now there’s an argument to have a few more players who are maybe a bit more established.’

Murphy has some sympathy for Kerkez but feels the Hungary international needs to get his head down and work on his composure if he is to make a success of his time at Liverpool.

‘He just lacks composure and quality in the final third when he gets there. Too often his final pass or his cross isn’t good enough,’ he continued.

‘He doesn’t have the composure of an Andy Robertson, and to be fair to him, you are filling the boots of arguably one of the best left-backs Liverpool’s ever had.”

‘I think the lack of quality at times is due to the fact he’s very fast. He’s very much 100 miles an hour. I’m surprised they’re not working with him more to slow him down in those areas and to just calm himself.

‘Now it wouldn’t be as bad if he was brilliant defensively, but he’s struggling defensively as well. His positional play is sometimes a bit off, he’s a bit erratic in terms of diving in or getting beat.

‘He likes jumping into people. It’s a dilemma for Liverpool, and I think one that they’ll definitely be looking at and trying to address, because not every signing works out.’

On Kerkez, Murphy went on: ‘I was somebody who saw him that year at Bournemouth and thought he looked like a terrific young player.

‘But the one thing that people don’t understand and it’s only when you’ve been in that position you can empathise with going from playing in one environment to being in the intense, magnified world of Liverpool Football Club.

‘Every game, every minute, every mistake is analysed by the fans, by the press, by the worldwide audience, and I think that expectation, and that pressure is a bit much for him.’

#1925. Angry Manchester United fans react to Michael Carrick sacking as new statement sent

The Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) have hit out at the club’s owners after Michael Carrick’s sacking marked another “depressing moment” at Old Trafford.

Carrick was relieved of his duties on Thursday morning, with United sitting 18th in the Premier League table after one win from their opening 10 matches.

It is expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as his replacement, though the timing of that has been complicated slightly by it being an international break and the USA preparing for two important Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti.

Confirmation of Carrick’s sacking came after United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco on Wednesday to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

The MUST paid tribute to Carrick, who won five Premier League titles with United as a player, as the group instead took aim at Ratcliffe and the club’s majority owners, the Glazers.

“Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United,” an MUST statement read.

“We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.

“The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.

“They lie with the ownership. The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.”

The United fans had continued to stick with Carrick, even as results collapsed in recent weeks.

After the 3-0 defeat at home by Bournemouth last month, the Stretford End sung Carrick’s name as he made his way off the pitch.

“The earlier Stretford End banner declaring, ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace’ was a warning,” the MUST continued in their criticism of ownership.

“The unprecedented scale of the booing at Old Trafford, alongside public criticism from senior players in recent weeks, now points to a deeper deterioration.

“These are signs of a club becoming more divided, with the bond between supporters, players and those running Manchester United under increasing strain.”

No senior figures at United put their name to the official statement confirming Carrick’s sacking.

The MUST urged United executives to put greater emphasis on accountability to help improve the relationship between fans and those running the club.

“I’m proud of my players. The most important thing was to be competitive, I said it before the match. If we approach every game like this, we’re one step closer to winning them all.

“There are times when you manage to play really well, but there are also times when we changed our approach and were strong on second balls and played a different kind of football. And that’s what great teams do: they play differently within the same game. I’m really pleased with my players today.”

“What I can say is that we can win every game, but I can’t guarantee we’ll reach that level of confidence by the end of the season. I don’t feel like we’ve got that kind of consistency yet.

“And I don’t want to say anything more than ‘we can win the next game’. Because that’s the feeling I get when I look at the team. But it depends on many things. If we’d had everyone available, we would definitely have been better in the Europa League, too.

“This run of matches has been tough for us with everything that’s happened. But I can say that if we’re competitive, then we can win every game in the league. Let’s focus on that and take it one day at a time.”

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like you did on Thursday and then turn on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

How is Gonçalo Ramos’ development going? He got an assist today…

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1922. Harry Kane sends message to Manchester United over Mauricio Pochettino move

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Harry Kane believes Manchester United will gain a ‘fantastic manager’ in Mauricio Pochettino if Michael Carrick is sacked.

United are expected to dismiss Carrick during the international break following the team’s worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa has left United 18th in the Premier League with just one win in 10 games. Carrick’s side are also out of the Carabao Cup following a 3-2 defeat at home to Brighton in September.

United have already reached an initial agreement with Pochettino, who is the head coach of the United States national side but has a $10 million (£7.4m) buyout clause in his contract, and the expectation is that the Argentine will be in place for United’s next Premier League fixture against Liverpool on November 22.

Kane worked alongside Pochettino for five years at Spurs where they reached a League Cup and Champions League final and has endorsed the 54-year-old’s likely move to United.

When asked about Pochettino’s potential move to Old Trafford on Wednesday, Kane said: ‘Me and Mauricio obviously have a fantastic relationship.

‘Obviously a fantastic coach, he’s managed the biggest clubs in the world. From my point of view, I can’t speak highly enough of him.

‘We’ll have to wait and see what happens but I know he’s a great guy but also a fantastic manager.’

#1921. Who will be on Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom team at Manchester United?

Manchester United are thrashing out the finer details of Mauricio Pochettino’s move to Old Trafford, with the Red Devils having to negotiate the bill to bring four of his trusted lieutenants back to England.

After identifying ex-Tottenham boss Pochettino as the desired replacement for sacked head coach Michael Carrick, Man Utd quickly agreed personal terms - before approaching the USA to extract their target from a four-year contract only signed following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It has been reported that the total compensation package United will have to pay the US Soccer Federation could be north of £10million, once fees for Pochettino’s staff have been agreed.

Assistant manager Jesus Perez has worked with Pochettino since his first job in management, employed initially as an analyst at Espanyol in LaLiga.

After building a strong relationship with Pochettino, Spaniard Perez was promoted to No2 when the Argentine was appointed manager of Southampton in 2013, and has been his assistant at every job since.

Perez and Pochettino joked about the United job during the World Cup, with the former apparently very keen on working at Old Trafford.

There are three other members of staff likely to make the move across the Atlantic. Miguel D’Agostino is a former team-mate of Pochettino’s, with the duo having played together at Newell’s Old Boys in their native Argentina.

Initially working as a scout for Pochettino at Espanyol, D’Agostino has also followed his compatriot from club to club since then.

Toni Jimenez is another to have worked with Pochettino at every club he has managed so far, plus the US national team. A goalkeeping coach, Jimenez first linked up with Pochettino in 2011 at Espanyol.

The final member of coaching staff mentioned in reports has not been involved in Pochettino’s setup as long as the others, but has a very close relationship to the former Chelsea manager.

#1918. International break dates 2027: Full calendar for next year

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 12:40

With a few fans and many critics, the FIFA international break will keep its reserved place in 2027, even without the biggest tournaments for Europeans and South Americans.

Next year maintains the new trend of 2026, which removed one of the breaks for international matches to create a longer period in which four matches can be accommodated instead of two.

Four dates will be set aside for international fixtures, one of them lasting 16 days, called the ‘Super FIFA Window’. All the others will last nine days, as usual. Brazilian football, however, will have one more because of the Women’s World Cup in the middle of the year.

22-30 March 7-15 June 20 September-5 October 8-16 November

The first FIFA window, in the third month of 2027, will feature several decisive fixtures around the world.

In Europe, the quarter-finals of the Nations League will be played, as will the Concacaf edition for the teams of North and Central America. The teams that are eliminated should look for friendlies against South American teams, as in June.

Also in March, Asian teams will begin qualifying for the 2030 World Cup and the 2031 Asian Cup. In Africa, the teams qualifying for the Africa Cup of Nations, which will be played in the middle of the year, when the Concacaf Gold Cup also takes place, will be decided.

The June FIFA window should be almost entirely friendlies, with the exception of the Nations League finals.

In September, South American World Cup qualifiers are expected to begin, although this has not yet been confirmed, and would also occupy the calendar in November. In Europe, countries will play qualification for Euro 2028.

Outside the FIFA windows, there will also be the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia, which was scheduled for the start of the year but was postponed to be played between 23 December and 21 January 2028 because of conflicts in the Middle East. European clubs, which will be in the middle of next season, will be affected by the absence of players who will be at the tournament.

England’s calendar in 2027 will be shaped by the Nations League and qualifying for Euro 2028. Thomas Tuchel’s side are in Group A3 with Spain, Croatia and Czechia, and the group winner will go through to the quarter-finals in March 2027.

England still have two group games to play, against Croatia at Wembley on 12 November and away to Spain on 15 November. The Nations League finals are scheduled for 9-13 June 2027, with the host nation yet to be confirmed.

Euro 2028 will be played in the United Kingdom and Ireland from 9 June to 9 July 2028. The qualifying draw takes place in Belfast on 6 December 2026, with fixtures running from March to November 2027 and play-offs in March 2028. As co-hosts, England must still qualify, although UEFA has reserved two automatic places for host nations.

2028: 20-28 March 29 May-6 June June/July: Copa America and European Championship 18 September-3 October 13-21 November

2029: 19-27 March 4-12 June 29 September-9 October 12-20 November

2030: 18-26 March 3-11 June June/July: World Cup 23 September-8 October 11-19 November

#1917. Manchester United recruitment team should be ‘sacked’ over £50m transfer, says Jamie Redknapp

Jamie Redknapp says Andrey Santos is ‘not a Manchester United player’ and claims whoever was responsible for his signing ‘deserves the sack’.

Desperate for midfield reinforcements over the summer, United spent £50m to sign Brazil international Santos from Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Manchester United made midfield targets their priority after Casemiro left Old Trafford and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious injury at the World Cup.

Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans joined Michael Carrick’s squad on top of Santos but all three midfielders have made inauspicious starts to their United careers.

Santos has earned just seven starts for a Manchester United team sitting in the relegation zone heading into the international break.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Redknapp doubts the 22-year-old Brazilian is at the level required to play for United and says bringing him to the club was a ‘sackable offence’ by those in charge at Old Trafford.

‘Can I throw one player at you? And this is no disrespect to the boy, because he’s not a bad player, but whoever brought in Andrey Santos, that for me is a sackable offence,’ Redknapp said on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas.

‘He is not a Manchester United player. He’s a decent player, he’s okay. But they brought [Youri] Tielemans in just after it.

‘What makes them think, “Okay, I’m going to get two midfield players”, when I’ve got [Kobbie] Mainoo there – three very similar players that haven’t got any athleticism to get round the pitch?’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

When it was point to him that Manchester United’s director of recruitment Christopher Vivell knew Santos from his previous spell at Chelsea, Redknapp added: ‘Even worse, then. I’d let them off the hook if they didn’t know him.’

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has also criticised Manchester United’s pursuit of Santos, who made just 47 appearances for Chelsea.

‘I’m not sure Andrey Santos was the right signing for Manchester United at £50m,’ Gerrard said last month.

‘I just think to play in Manchester United’s midfield every single game, every single weekend, you’d expect to compete for the Premier League and the Champions League.

‘Santos, he’s a good player, but for me, he’s not a Manchester United player. I think he’s a bit short, that would be my opinion. United’s midfield is way off the level, it’s way off.’

United’s dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost former England midfielder Carrick his job at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino, the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss, is the frontrunner to take over at Manchester United.

If appointed, Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils would be a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool after the international break.

Chelsea have been urged to sign ‘top-class’ Trent Alexander-Arnold in January following a frustrating start to his Real Madrid career.

Scotland and North Macedonia will clash at Hampden Park on Friday night in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts are third in the standings with four points, while the visitors are bottom of the table and yet to pick up a single point from four matches.

Since replacing long-serving manager Steve Clarke, who stepped down at the end of a disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, new boss Sebastian Pocognoli has endured a mixed start to life in charge.

Pocognoli has guided Scotland to just one win from four Nations League fixtures, beating Friday's visitors 2-1, alongside a 0-0 draw with Slovenia, a 3-0 defeat to Switzerland and, most recently, a 2-1 defeat against Slovenia.

Scotland, as a result, sit third in League B Group 1 with four points, leaving them four points above bottom-placed North Macedonia and three points behind second-placed Slovenia in the promotion-playoff place, while leaders Switzerland are out of reach with only two games remaining.

With Scotland hoping to secure a second-placed finish and promotion playoff place, Pocognoli's side will be desperate to secure all three points on Friday to potentially move level with Slovenia, who face Switzerland.

Despite their struggles in the group campaign, including scoring only three goals across four matches, Scotland will draw confidence from their dominant 2-0 win in the reverse fixture against North Macedonia, when they took 25 shots and had seven big chances compared to their opponents' nine shots and zero big chances.

North Macedonia also head into Friday's encounter enduring a miserable five-game losing streak and 12-game winless run across all competitions.

Adding to their concerning form, North Macedonia have failed to score in 10 of those matches, including each of their last eight outings.

Goce Sedloski, who took charge in December 2025, is, therefore, still searching for his first win as North Macedonia manager, and he will be desperate to finally secure a victory on Friday.

The visitors will have to improve across all areas of the pitch if they are to secure any points, having failed to score and conceded 10 goals in their four Nations League games.

A victory will also be required for North Macedonia to have any chance of avoiding a relegation playoff match, with three points and at least a draw, with Scotland losing both remaining matches and a significant swing in goal difference, needed to climb to third.

Scotland are boosted by the return of Scott McTominay, who did not feature in the first four Nations League matches due to undergoing heart surgery.

The midfielder is expected to return straight into the starting 11, providing attacking support for Oli McBurnie, with John McGinn, Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour featuring in midfield.

At the back, Aaron Hickey could start on the right of a back-three, alongside Jack Hendry and Luis Binks, while Ben Gannon-Doak and Andy Robertson provide width from wing-back.

As for North Macedonia, captain Enis Bardhi should start in attacking midfield, with Ljupche Doriev and Dimitar Mitrovski providing support from the wings for striker Elmin Rastoder.

Further back, Eljif Elmas and Jani Atanasov should start at the base of midfield, with Visar Misliu and Anes Meljichi starting in central defence.

Gunn; Hickey, Hendry, Binks; Doak, McGinn, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McTominay; McBurnie

North Macedonia possible starting lineup:

Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Meljichi, Misliu, Alioski; Elmas, Atanasov, Mitrovski, Bardhi, Doriev; Rastoder

Scotland may be enduring a difficult run, but they demonstrated their superiority over the struggling North Macedonia in the reverse fixture and should secure another comfortable win on Friday.

#1912. Johan Manzambi injury update as Aston Villa star sent home from international duty

Johan Manzambi has been forced to withdraw from Switzerland duty due to injury, raising concerns over the midfielder’s availability for Aston Villa in the coming weeks.

A £60million summer signing from Freiburg, Manzambi has returned to Aston Villa for further assessments on a calf issue.

According to the Swiss football federation, Manzambi joined up with the national team already carrying a knock which is said to have been sustained during Aston Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United.

Manzambi was forced off at Old Trafford in the 78th minute following a strong challenge from Manchester United defender Leny Yoro.

Despite the knock, Manzambi was still called up for Switzerland’s Nations League games against Slovenia and Scotland. But it has now been decided not to risk the 21-year-old, with Manzambi sent back to Villa to continue his recovery.

A statement from the Swiss FA read: “Johan Manzambi has been ruled out of the upcoming Nations League matches against Slovenia and Scotland.

“The midfielder joined the national team camp on Monday with a calf injury.

“Despite intensive medical treatment and further examinations, his condition has not improved sufficiently, making him unavailable for either game.

“In agreement with Aston Villa, Manzambi will therefore return to his club on Friday.”

Manzambi has quickly established himself in Unai Emery’s team, producing two goals and three assists in six Premier League starts this term.

#1911. Mikel Arteta urged to sell £60m Arsenal star in swap deal for Julian Alvarez

Alan Smith believes that Arsenal should consider offering Martin Zubimendi to Atletico Madrid as part of a swap deal to sign Julian Alvarez.

Zubimendi’s future at Arsenal has come into question in recent weeks, with the Spaniard still yet to start a Premier League match this season.

The central midfielder made an immediate impact after signing from Real Sociedad for £60million 18 months ago, starting 34 matches as Mikel Arteta’s side ended their 22-year wait for another league title.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi at the end of last season and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly, who started in his place in the Champions League final.

Lewis-Skelly’s continued form, as well as the high-profile summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, has seen Zubimendi slide down the pecking order in north London and sparked speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Atletico Madrid are reportedly keen to bring Zubimendi back to La Liga, and Smith believes the Gunners can use that interest to finally strike a deal for Alvarez, who they were heavily interested in over the summer.

‘Obviously he played a big part last season, but having been an ever-present, he might be getting a bit restless not to be getting starts, just to be coming off the bench for a few minutes, Smith told Best Betting Sites.

‘So that might be something that can be part of a bargaining chip for Arsenal.

‘If you could do a part swap, then obviously you’re not shelling out over 100 million pounds on Alvarez, because I’m sure Atletico would want something well in excess of that. So that might be a way forward.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Looking at his games this season, he’s only got a couple of goals for Atletico. But he’s 26 years old, he’s got some good years ahead of him, and he’s got plenty of energy. So to me, he still looks like the most suitable target for Arsenal.’

On Zubimendi’s quiet start to the season, the former Arsenal striker added: ‘It’s a strange one. I don’t know what’s happened, whether Arteta has decided he wants a different sort of midfielder.

‘Obviously, Lewis-Skelly’s coming into the reckoning, and Guimaraes, who’s a totally different player to Zubimendi, he’s more dynamic, more likely to get you a goal.’

Zubimendi has also been linked with a move to Chelsea, but the Arsenal midfielder was keen to pour cold water on any speculation linking him with a move away from the Emirates in the upcoming window.

‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

#1910. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.
